offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

first_checks: Check whether webhook-receiver is up and answering. Look at its recent responses: rising 4xx/5xx or timeouts. Look especially for signature-verification failures (wrong or rotated secret).
Check that webhook-receiver can produce to provider-events. A broker that is down or slow, or produce errors, would stop it from acking.
On the provider side, look at the unacknowledged webhooks: when the oldest was first sent, its retry count, and its last error. This shows when the problem started and whether it is still growing.
If webhooks are being acked but the books still lag, check the consumer-group lag and errors for ledger-consumer and payment-confirmer on provider-events.
triage.if_false: The alert is false if the provider shows few or no unacked webhooks up to the cutoff, webhook-receiver is acking normally, and a fresh money check settles within 15 s. A cutoff set ahead of the provider's clock, or a money check misreading the provider's records, would also make it false.

findings.cause: At 21:25:08 webhook-receiver was redeployed with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, and no other service changed. From then on it refuses the provider's webhooks with 'signature mismatch'. The likely reason is that the provider still signs with the secret the receiver used before; that is inferred, because the provider's secret cannot be seen. The receiver does not acknowledge refused webhooks, so the provider keeps resending them. Unacknowledged webhooks therefore pile up and never reach provider-events or the ledger, and the money check cannot settle up to its cutoff. The bad_signature rate climbs with the retries, while queued webhooks drop off. The backlog is growing: 133 at the alert, 276 at c8.

evidence.shows: All containers are running and healthy, Kafka and both consumers included. webhook-receiver alone was started later, at 21:25:08, than the rest (21:23:4x).
Only webhook-receiver was redeployed recently, at 21:25:08 with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, on the same image as before. No other service's settings changed.
result=bad_signature first appears just after the redeploy (2.75/s at 21:25:32) and rises to 13.58/s by 21:26:32. result=queued falls from about 2.3/s to 0.96/s.
webhook-receiver logs 'webhook refused: bad signature', reason 'signature mismatch', many times a second at 21:26:34. These are WARNING level, which is why c3's ERROR/WARN filter returned nothing.
The total webhook rate rose from 0.4/s to 12.8/s after 21:25, which is consistent with the provider retrying refused deliveries.
A fresh money check could not run: after 20 s it had not settled, with 276 webhooks not acknowledged by our receiver. That confirms the alert's symptom and shows the backlog growing from 133.

findings.left_open: The tools do not show which secret version the provider signs with, so it is not confirmed that the provider still uses v1. A wrong or missing v2 secret value in the receiver would also explain the mismatches. The HTTP status the receiver returns on a refusal was not checked. Some webhooks are still being queued (about 1/s); whether these were signed with a matching secret, or are leftovers from before the redeploy, is unclear. Kafka produce and consumer lag were not checked directly, but the receiver itself refusing the webhooks is enough to explain the alert.
